newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says old age cannot dim religious energies.
newsitem.headline: Pope says old age cannot dim religious energies.

text.p: Pope John Paul, still recovering from an operation to remove his appendix last month, told fellow priests on Thursday that his religious energies could not be dimmed by the effects of old age.

"With the passing of years the body's strength slowly ebbs away," the 76-year-old Pope said in a homily during evening prayers celebrating his 50 years as a priest with other clerics ordained into the Roman Catholic Church in the same year.
"But the interior force does not follow the laws of physics," the Polish-born pontiff added. "Priesthood, in fact, cannot be reduced to merely functional aspects.
"We are ministers of Christ...and, for the time that God wills, a formidable task still awaits us.
"Difficulties and tests will never discourage us nor will we be tempted to repeat the lament of Jeremiah: 'Ah, Lord God! Look, I cannot speak: for I am old,'" the Pope said.
The Pope has had a string of health problems recently and has frequently looked tired during public appearances.
On Thursday he looked well, although his left hand trembled as he delivered his homily in the Vatican's cavernous Pope Paul VI auditorium, where he regularly holds general audiences.
The Vatican has not denied a string of media reports that the Pope may be suffering from a neurological disorder.
Some progressive Catholics have openly suggested that the Pope should consider resigning instead of reigning for life as Roman pontiffs traditionally do.
Vatican officials have dismissed talk of resignation and the Pope's comments on Thursday clearly emphasised that.
Looking back on his 50 years in the priesthood, the Pope recalled his childhood in Poland and remembered his family and close friends -- observing that most were now dead.
"I have close to my heart and am grateful to all those who helped lead me to the altar," the Pontiff said.
"So many people dear to me; men and women, learned and simple! Most are now in eternity," he added.
The Pope, elected in 1978 as the first non-Italian Pontiff in 450 years, was 26 years old when he became a priest on November 1, 1946 in the city of Krakow.
He had just been through the ravages of World War Two and had already lost all the members of his immediate family.

He has invited priests from around the world who were ordained in the same year for celebratory services this week. He will lead a special mass with fellow jubilee priests at St Peter's Basilica on Sunday.
